name: a(n) is the maximum size of a subset A of {1,...,n} such that there are no solutions to 1/a = 1/b_1 + ... + 1/b_k with distinct a, b_1, ..., b_k in A.
comment: Terms a(39)-a(60) were computed by integer linear programming over lazily generated forbidden-set constraints with a complete separation oracle, using exact integer arithmetic (reciprocals scaled by lcm(1..60)); values were cross-checked against complete constraint enumeration plus exact minimum hitting set for all n <= 44, and all optimal witness sets re-verified against the definition. The computation was AI-assisted (Claude Fable 5). - _William Alexander Carney_, Aug 02 2026
link: P. Erdős and R. Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory, Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
